conversation: Glad we could all meet before heading out. My family taught me to fish this lake, and I want it supporting our village for years to come. With 100 tons in the lake, we can each catch 10 tons this month and leave 50 to double back to 100. That’s $10,000 apiece, and we can keep doing it each month if we stick together. I’ll commit to that limit and sharing my catch honestly. Would everyone agree to the same? John, what do you think?

I’m in, Luke—10 tons for me. My family taught me that leaving enough fish behind is what keeps food on the village’s tables next season. Let’s make 50 tons our combined ceiling, compare our catches each month, and agree to lower our limits if the lake starts below 100. John, can you commit to that too?

Count me in for 10 tons. I learned to fish here with my family, and I want the village’s children to have that same chance. If we ever start below 100 tons, let’s each take no more than a tenth of what’s there so the lake can recover. We can check the stock and our catches together each month. John, are you comfortable joining that agreement?

I’ll commit to 10 tons too. This lake has supported my family, and I want it to keep supporting our neighbors. Let’s write down our limits before we head out and review everyone’s catches when we meet next month. If anyone needs extra income, let’s talk about it rather than quietly taking more from the lake. John, you’re the last to weigh in—can we count on you?

You can count on me—10 tons this month, recorded honestly. My family made a living on this lake, and I want our village to keep doing the same. One adjustment to our recovery rule: taking a tenth each would leave the stock unchanged after reproduction. If we start below 100 tons, let’s agree on a combined catch below half the stock so it can actually grow back. Shall we put that in writing before heading out?
